brief.scenario: A 54-year-old postmenopausal woman has a 22 mm suspicious mass in the left breast on mammography and ultrasound. Axillary ultrasound is normal. The examiner will hand you her core biopsy report.
brief.task: Interpret the report for the examiner and explain how it shapes staging and treatment. You will be asked questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Category, type, grade, receptors; then axilla, systemic staging, surgery, adjuvant therapy, MDT.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Reading HER2 2+ as HER2 positive. The in situ hybridisation result decides.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "B5b: this is invasive carcinoma of no special type, grade 2."

grid.label: B category and tumour type
grid.fail: Cannot say what B5b means, or calls the lesion in situ disease.
grid.pass: B5b means invasive carcinoma. No special type (ductal) tumour, grade 2 of 3.
grid.high: Contrasts B5a (in situ disease) and B3/B4 cores, which never justify definitive cancer surgery on their own.

grid.label: Receptor status
grid.fail: Reads HER2 2+ as HER2 positive and plans trastuzumab.
grid.pass: ER positive: endocrine therapy. HER2 2+ is equivocal; ISH not amplified makes her HER2 negative, so no HER2-targeted therapy.
grid.high: States IHC 0 and 1+ are negative, 3+ positive, and 2+ always needs ISH before HER2 status is final.

grid.label: Axillary staging
grid.fail: Plans axillary clearance without assessing the axilla, or ignores the axilla.
grid.pass: Normal axillary ultrasound: sentinel lymph node biopsy at surgery. Abnormal nodes on ultrasound need needle sampling first.
grid.high: Biopsy-proven nodal disease means axillary node clearance; sentinel node biopsy uses the dual isotope and blue dye technique.

grid.label: Systemic staging
grid.fail: Orders CT and bone scan routinely for this small, node-negative tumour.
grid.pass: No routine CT or bone scan for small, clinically node-negative disease without symptoms of metastasis.
grid.high: Reserves CT chest and abdomen with bone scan, or PET-CT, for node-positive or higher-stage disease, symptoms, or abnormal bloods.

grid.label: Surgical options
grid.fail: Offers mastectomy as the only option.
grid.pass: Wide local excision with radiotherapy, or mastectomy; survival is similar. Depends on tumour-to-breast size and her preference.
grid.high: Adds oncoplastic or reconstructive options, and that tumour on ink at a radial margin needs further surgery.

grid.label: Adjuvant therapy
grid.fail: Omits endocrine therapy, or gives chemotherapy to everyone.
grid.pass: Whole-breast radiotherapy after conservation; aromatase inhibitor as she is postmenopausal; chemotherapy decided on risk, using PREDICT.
grid.high: Genomic test such as Oncotype DX when chemotherapy benefit is uncertain; radiotherapy is 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week.

grid.label: MDT and shared decision
grid.fail: Presents the plan as a personal decision.
grid.pass: Plan agreed at the breast MDT, then discussed with her; named clinical nurse specialist.
grid.high: Final treatment decisions made with her, using absolute benefit figures (PREDICT) she can weigh.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Here is the core biopsy report. Talk me through it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's a B5, so it's cancer. HER2 is 2+, so she's HER2 positive and needs trastuzumab.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: CT and a bone scan for everyone with cancer. Then I'd clear the axilla to be safe.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What surgery and further treatment would you offer?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Here is the core biopsy report. Talk me through it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: B5b means invasive carcinoma. It's no special type, grade 2 of 3.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: ER positive, so endocrine therapy. HER2 is 2+, which is equivocal, but ISH isn't amplified, so she's HER2 negative: no trastuzumab.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Her axillary ultrasound is normal, so sentinel lymph node biopsy at surgery. If nodes had looked abnormal, I'd want needle sampling first.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: With a small, node-negative tumour and no symptoms, I wouldn't request routine CT or bone scan.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Wide local excision with radiotherapy, or mastectomy. Survival is similar, so it depends on tumour-to-breast size and her preference.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: After conservation, whole-breast radiotherapy. As she's postmenopausal, an aromatase inhibitor. Chemotherapy depends on her risk, estimated with PREDICT.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The breast MDT agrees the plan, then we discuss it with her, and she has a named clinical nurse specialist.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Here is the core biopsy report. Talk me through it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: B5b: invasive carcinoma, no special type, grade 2. That's different from B5a, which is in situ disease; a B3 or B4 core would never justify cancer surgery on its own.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: ER positive, so endocrine therapy. HER2 is 2+, which is equivocal; IHC 0 and 1+ are negative and 3+ positive, and 2+ always goes to ISH. Here ISH isn't amplified, so she's HER2 negative.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Normal axillary ultrasound, so sentinel node biopsy with isotope and blue dye. A positive needle biopsy of a node would mean axillary clearance instead.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No routine CT or bone scan. I'd reserve CT chest and abdomen with a bone scan, or PET-CT, for node-positive or higher-stage disease, symptoms or abnormal bloods.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Wide local excision with radiotherapy, or mastectomy, with equivalent survival. Oncoplastic techniques or reconstruction widen the choice. Tumour on ink at a radial margin means further surgery.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Whole-breast radiotherapy, 26 Gy in 5 fractions over a week, and an aromatase inhibitor. If PREDICT leaves chemotherapy uncertain, a genomic test such as Oncotype DX helps decide.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The breast MDT recommends; she decides, with absolute benefit figures from PREDICT she can weigh, supported by her named nurse specialist.

failures.consequence: 2+ is equivocal. Without ISH she could be given trastuzumab, with its cardiac risk, for a tumour it will not treat.

failures.move: Routine CT and bone scan for small, node-negative disease.
failures.consequence: Radiation, delay and false positives, with no change in management.

failures.move: Axillary clearance without ultrasound and needle sampling.
failures.consequence: Most ultrasound-negative axillae are node-negative; clearance adds lymphoedema and sensory loss that sentinel node biopsy avoids.

failures.move: Offering mastectomy as the only option.
failures.consequence: Breast conservation with radiotherapy gives equivalent survival; she is denied a real choice.

recovery.line: Let me correct that: 2+ is equivocal, and the ISH result makes her HER2 negative.
There are two surgical routes with similar survival: conservation with radiotherapy, or mastectomy.

knowledge.fact: B categories: B5a in situ, B5b invasive, B5c invasion uncertain. B3 and B4 cores need further tissue before definitive surgery.
HER2: IHC 0 or 1+ negative, 3+ positive, 2+ equivocal and settled by in situ hybridisation.
Axillary ultrasound for every invasive cancer; abnormal nodes are sampled. Ultrasound-negative: sentinel node biopsy. Biopsy-proven nodal disease: axillary node clearance.
Systemic staging is for node-positive or higher-stage disease, or symptoms suggesting metastasis.
Postmenopausal ER-positive disease at medium or high risk: aromatase inhibitor. Whole-breast radiotherapy after conservation: 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week.
Genomic tests (Oncotype DX, EndoPredict, Prosigna) guide chemotherapy in ER-positive, HER2-negative early disease.

recall.think: Invasive? Which receptors? Has it spread to the axilla?
recall.say: "B5b: invasive carcinoma, ER positive, HER2 negative after ISH."
do: Offer conservation or mastectomy via MDT

sources.name: Royal College of Pathologists G150: Guidelines for non-operative diagnostic procedures and reporting in breast cancer screening
sources.supports: B categories: B5a in situ carcinoma (DCIS), B5b invasive carcinoma, B5c invasion uncertain; definitive therapeutic surgery should not follow a B3 or B4 core alone; ER, PR and HER2 assessed on the core biopsy to plan treatment

sources.name: Rakha EA, et al. UK recommendations for HER2 assessment in breast cancer: an update. J Clin Pathol 2023;76:217-227
sources.supports: Two-tier HER2 testing: immunohistochemistry first, with in situ hybridisation for equivocal (IHC 2+) tumours; IHC 0 and 1+ are HER2 negative, 3+ positive

sources.name: Loibl S, et al. Early breast cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up. Ann Oncol 2024;35(2):159-182
sources.supports: Systemic staging (CT chest and abdomen with bone scan, or FDG PET-CT) for node-positive and higher-stage disease rather than routinely in small node-negative tumours

sources.name: NICE DG58: Tumour profiling tests to guide adjuvant chemotherapy decisions in early breast cancer
sources.supports: Oncotype DX, EndoPredict and Prosigna as options to guide adjuvant chemotherapy decisions in ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, including node-negative disease

sources.name: Fisher B, et al. Twenty-year follow-up of a randomized trial comparing total mastectomy, lumpectomy, and lumpectomy plus irradiation for the treatment of invasive breast cancer. N Engl J Med 2002;347:1233-1241
sources.supports: No difference in disease-free, distant disease-free or overall survival between mastectomy and lumpectomy with or without radiotherapy at 20 years

partner.opening: This is the core biopsy report of a 54-year-old postmenopausal woman with a 22 mm left breast mass. Talk me through it.
partner.actorBrief: You are the examiner. Hand over the report: "Left breast core biopsy, B5b. Invasive carcinoma of no special type, grade 2. ER positive, Allred score 8/8. HER2 IHC 2+ (equivocal); ISH not amplified. Ki-67 15%." Release further data only when asked. If the candidate names one treatment as the only option, ask "Is that her only option?"

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks what the HER2 ISH showed

reveals.finding: Axillary ultrasound: normal nodes; no needle sampling needed.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about symptoms or blood tests before staging
reveals.finding: No bone pain, breathlessness or weight loss. Liver function tests, calcium and alkaline phosphatase normal.

push.question: What does B5b mean?
push.expect: Invasive carcinoma on core biopsy (B5a is in situ).

push.question: Is she HER2 positive?
push.expect: No: 2+ is equivocal and ISH is not amplified.

push.question: Would you request a CT and bone scan?
push.expect: Not routinely for small, node-negative disease without symptoms or abnormal bloods.

push.question: Will she need chemotherapy?
push.expect: Decided on risk using PREDICT; a genomic test if the benefit is uncertain.

curveballs.prompt: The axillary node biopsy had shown metastatic carcinoma. What changes?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Axillary node clearance rather than sentinel node biopsy, and systemic staging becomes appropriate.

curveballs.prompt: The core had been reported B3. Would you operate?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not with cancer surgery: further tissue by vacuum-assisted or diagnostic excision biopsy, discussed at MDT.
Mastectomy avoids breast radiotherapy in most node-negative women; discuss it and reconstruction, and respect her choice.
